page.layout: One column of text. Latin paragraphs at the top and bottom, with an indented Syriac passage in the middle. Page number at the head. Catchword at the foot right. No margin notes.

main_text.p: piat famulum hunc suum ab hac grauissima, afflictione. O Domina semper virgo, refugium fidelium, & fortissimum nostrum seruorum tuorum auxilium, tuis intercessionibus libera famulum hunc tuum à præsenti afflictione.

Maronitæ, qui Syri sunt, & Syriaca in sacris functionibus utuntur lingua, obiasque quoque eiusmodi ad B. Virginem Mariam, aliosque Sanctos formulas habent, ex quibus paucas. In Proœmio primæ stationis Nocturni Dominicæ simplicis Officij sic ad B. Virginem orant:
Te autem supplicamus, o mater vitæ, & fons lætitiarum, ut quemadmo-

page.notes: The Syriac passage (Maronite prayer to the Blessed Virgin) could not be read letter by letter at this scan resolution, so each line is marked illegible; the number of lines is estimated. The first Latin word "piat" is a fragment from "placeat" at the page head, kept as printed. The word "quemadmo-" is broken at the line end; the catchword "mo-" continues it on the next page.
